package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of these packages contain vulnerabilities that allow attackers to craft malicious npm package archives with directory traversal or symlink entries. When such packages are installed or extracted, the vulnerable extraction logic can write files or create symlinks outside the intended node_modules directory, potentially overwriting sensitive system files and enabling arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running npm install, even if lifecycle scripts are disabled.

execution_context.trigger: During package extraction (postinstall or npm install)
execution_context.file_location: npm package archive (.tar.gz/.tgz) containing file entries with directory traversal sequences

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package extraction, the extraction logic processes archive entries containing directory traversal sequences (e.g., ../../), interprets the path, and writes the file to a location outside the intended node_modules directory, resulting in the potential overwrite of sensitive system files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Archive entries with directory traversal sequences are a well-known technique for escaping the intended extraction directory, allowing attackers to overwrite arbitrary files on the filesystem.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package extraction should strictly confine all written files to the target directory (e.g., node_modules/package_name). Malicious behavior occurs when extraction code fails to sanitize or validate file paths, enabling writes outside this directory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate npm package archives should never contain file paths with directory traversal sequences (../) or absolute paths that escape the package directory.
key_indicators: Archive entries with '../' in file paths
Extraction code that does not normalize and validate file paths before writing
Files written outside the node_modules or intended extraction directory during npm install

execution_context.trigger: During package extraction (postinstall or npm install)
execution_context.file_location: npm package archive (.tar.gz/.tgz) containing symlink entries

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package extraction, the extraction logic processes symlink entries that point to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd), creates the symlink within the extraction directory, and allows subsequent archive entries to overwrite the target of the symlink, resulting in the potential modification of system files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Symlink entries in archives that point to absolute paths or sensitive system files are a known attack vector for file overwrite and privilege escalation, as they can redirect writes to unintended locations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal extraction should only allow symlinks that point within the package directory. Allowing symlinks to point outside the extraction directory or to system files violates security boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate npm packages may use symlinks, but these should only reference files within the package directory and never point to system files or parent directories.
key_indicators: Symlink entries in archives with targets outside the extraction directory
Symlink targets that are absolute paths (e.g., /etc/passwd) or contain directory traversal sequences
Extraction code that does not restrict symlink targets to within the package directory
Creation of symlinks during npm install that point to sensitive system locations

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious npm package archive containing file entries with directory traversal sequences or symlink entries pointing to sensitive system files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious archive is published to npm or distributed directly to victims.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious package using npm CLI, triggering the extraction of the archive by the vulnerable tar or @npmcli/arborist package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extraction logic in tar/arborist processes malicious file paths and symlink entries.

attack_chain.action: Extraction logic fails to properly sanitize file paths and symlink targets, allowing files to be written or symlinks to be created outside the intended node_modules directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary files, including sensitive system files, may be overwritten or modified, potentially leading to code execution or system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction during npm install with file paths containing '../' or absolute paths
Creation of symlinks during npm package extraction that point outside the node_modules or intended extraction directory
Unexpected file overwrites or modifications outside the node_modules directory during npm install, especially targeting system files
file_indicators: npm package archives (.tar.gz/.tgz) containing file entries with '../' in their paths
npm package archives with file entries using absolute paths (e.g., /etc/passwd)
Symlink entries in npm package archives with targets pointing to system files or outside the package directory
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package extraction for archive entries containing directory traversal sequences (../) or absolute paths, and for symlink entries with targets outside the intended extraction directory. Flag or block packages that attempt to write files outside the node_modules directory or create symlinks to sensitive system locations. Employ file system monitoring during npm install to detect unexpected file writes or symlink creations outside the package directory. Ensure use of patched versions of tar and @npmcli/arborist that enforce strict path and symlink validation.
